Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509

Class X509LoginMethodFragment

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.x509.X509LoginMethodFragment
All Implemented Interfaces:
LoginMethodFragment
public class X509LoginMethodFragment extends Object implements LoginMethodFragment
Contributes the sign-in with a client certificate to the login page: a form with one button that posts, with the CSRF token, to POST /login/x509. The template reads action() through this bean, because where the form posts depends on the transport:
  • with a proxy that forwards the certificate, the proxy fronts the whole application, so the form posts to the relative path, on the origin of the page;
  • with only the dedicated TLS port, the certificate is requested by that port alone, so a page served on any other port posts to the same host on that port over https; a page already served on that port posts to the relative path.
The session cookie and the CSRF token stay valid on the other port (cookies belong to a host, not to a port), but a browser only sends a cookie with a SameSite restriction on a post between pages of the same site, and it counts http and https as different sites: the main port must be served over https too, or the login page must be opened on the TLS port. The bean only exists while the sign-in with a certificate is enabled.
